# Causalia

> Deterministic simulation testing for concurrent and distributed .NET software. Causalia makes timing, retry, duplicate-delivery, partial-persistence, restart and concurrency failures reproducible.

Causalia is an open-source MIT-licensed .NET 10 project. Use it when correctness depends on execution ordering or partial failure. It complements unit, integration and end-to-end tests; it does not replace real-provider verification or performance testing.

## Start here

- [Causalia homepage](https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/Causalia/): Product overview, interactive Failure Lab, getting started, packages and FAQ.
- [README](https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Causalia/blob/main/README.md): Canonical installation and adoption documentation.
- [Scenario cookbook](https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Causalia/blob/main/SCENARIOS.md): Production-style recipes and advanced APIs.
- [AI agent guide](https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/Causalia/agents.html): Recommended inspect → model → explore → patch → replay workflow for coding agents.
- [Business value](https://pjotrcasteel.github.io/Causalia/business-value.html): Practical adoption and engineering-cost evaluation.
- [Example application](https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Causalia/tree/main/examples/Causalia.ExampleApp): Concrete .NET example.
- [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Causalia): Main package.
- [Source](https://github.com/pjotrcasteel/Causalia): Repository.

## Quick adoption

- Install the CLI: `dotnet tool install --global Causalia.Tool --version 2.1.1`
- Inspect a solution: `dotnet causalia inspect MyService.slnx`
- Structured inspection for automation/agents: `dotnet causalia inspect MyService.slnx --format json`
- Generate a first test project: `dotnet causalia init MyService.slnx`
- Install core: `dotnet add package Causalia --version 2.1.1`

## Use Causalia when

- retry or idempotency matters;
- messages may be delivered more than once;
- acknowledgements can be ambiguous;
- optimistic concurrency, CAS, ETags, leases or competing workers matter;
- inbox/outbox or workflow replay can happen;
- a process can restart after partial durable progress;
- eventual consistency or distributed invariants matter;
- a race is difficult to reproduce in a normal test runner.

## Do not infer

- A Causalia trace is reproducible evidence, not automatic root-cause proof.
- Simulated provider semantics do not certify a real provider.
- Causalia is not a replacement for real performance/load testing.
- Production code should generally remain independent of Causalia; prefer normal .NET seams such as TimeProvider, CancellationToken and narrow dependency interfaces.
